html:
I had just gone to bed when a colleague sent me a message:

Kobe died.



It didn’t feel like a joke. I quickly checked the news and confirmed it was true.

My heart raced. I felt so sad, as if I’d lost an old friend.

His life was glorious, and he inspired countless people, in basketball and far beyond it; that needs no retelling.

I just can’t get over how unpredictable life is. Someone so celebrated, so accomplished, only a few years into retirement, gone just like that, leaving a whole family behind.

Before a tragedy like this, everyone is equal, rich or poor, high or low.

And life is far too short. A tweet from Mark Cuban put it well:


Never forget how precious life is. Never let the people who mean the most to you forget how much you love them.

I’d add one more line: never forget how much they love you.

Remind yourself every moment to live only for yourself, and only for the people who love you and the people you love.

(I’ve just learned that one of his daughters was on the helicopter too. She was only 13… Rest in peace.)

That same morning he had been texting with Shaquille O’Neal’s son.

His last tweet was an exchange with LeBron James.

Doc Rivers in tears during an interview
